answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a kernel registration system, requiring each new identity to secure a unique sponsor who stakes an increasingly high fee based on prior registrations. For each additional new identity, this fee climbs by 50 tokens. The sponsor must also produce original work graded by a jury, which signals their legitimacy. If an identity fails, the sponsor loses their entire stake, akin to a glacier melting under pressure, where each fraudulent identity risks eroding substantial resources and complicating their financial landscape.
